scope: Separate reconstructed draft cattle and walking study for the supply wagon. Original approved Stampede geometry, skeleton, clips and native assets remain untouched.
date_location: Western United States trail freight, approximately 1865-1880; no named animal, exact breed pedigree or measured museum replica is claimed.

sources.claim: Two pairs of oxen pulled the lighter Murphy trail wagon discussed by NPS. Use four cattle with two neck yokes.

Ford's first-hand ox-driving account and photographs distinguish heavy wheel oxen from lean longhorn leaders. Red Durham cattle were used; the photographed modern team shows broad bodies, short horns and light facial markings. Wooden neck yokes have loose bent bows, pins and separate iron tongue/draft fittings. Draft force passes through a chain; the tongue steers and checks forward wagon movement.
sources.visual_evidence: Printed pages 4 and 9 rendered from the downloaded PDF and actually inspected on October 8. These are modern photographs of working cattle and reconstructed equipment, not period photographs.

sources.claim: Muybridge's c1881 nine-image Ox, walking plate supplies a near-period visual reference for short horns, piebald cattle and a grounded walk. The monochrome plate supplies no coat-colour evidence and no exact animation timing.

render_brief.appearance: Reconstructed broad-bodied red-and-white horned draft cattle. Create a separate derivative of the existing bovine mesh with a broader body and shorter horns. Retain the existing natural red-brown/white coat and dark hooves. Do not call the result an authenticated Durham or a named historical ox. No nose rings, modern tags, invented brands or decorative harness.
render_brief.motion: A new in-place four-beat walk with prolonged stance, short swing clearance, restrained body motion and no airborne gallop. Timing and stride length are animator reconstructions; verify grounded feet and distance-driven phase, not a claimed exact Muybridge reproduction.
render_brief.hitch: Two paired wooden neck yokes with loose U-bows and pins. The rear tongue passes through its ring behind the goose stop; a distinct draft chain connects wagon underframe and yokes. Check clearances across the full walk before native integration.
render_brief.colour: Natural red-brown and white cattle, warm wood and dark iron at full natural strength; no deliberate desaturation.
render_brief.people: No new person is rendered in this study.

history_lines: Oxen were cattle trained to work under a yoke.
Heavy wheel oxen steered and restrained the wagon.
This team and its walking gait are reconstructions.
review_required: Full gait contact and loop review
Yoke, horn, chain and tongue clearance
Native movement, cargo filtering, both directions and cleanup
